response: Global management of colorectal cancer (CRC) with synchronous liver metastases (SLM) at the same centre does not significantly influence overall survival. However, it is associated with fewer procedures. On the other hand, a staged management approach is associated with a longer delay and increased use of chemotherapy between procedures, suggesting that more rigorous selection of patients for surgery may explain the higher disease-free survival after SLM resection. Therefore, while global management at the same centre may not improve overall survival, it can lead to more efficient treatment with fewer procedures.
